desc:
The major theme Creation: The making of the heavens, the earth, the sea and all that is in them. A reading: every passage it names resolves to a verse in the Berean text.

**Doug Egge's note.** The theme is Creation: God's making and ordering of the world, "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth" (Gen 1:1), and every core concept below begins there. It also reaches forward, because later scripture carries the idea on, and Paul above all ties the first creation to a new one: "if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation" (2 Cor 5:17); "What counts is a new creation" (Gal 6:15); "The creation waits in eager expectation" and "will be set free from its bondage to decay" (Rom 8:19, 21); "All things were created through Him and for Him" (Col 1:16). Isaiah had already said "I will create new heavens and a new earth" (Isa 65:17), and the Bible ends "Behold, I make all things new" (Rev 21:5). The later passages extend the theme; they do not replace the original creation it is about. The graph's node for the word "creation" keeps to the word and does not join Genesis to Revelation on its own.
